**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore hybrid vector search, prompt injection defenses, and semantic LLM caching.

learningJourney.title: What is a Production RAG Retrieval Pipeline
learningJourney.explanation:
A production RAG pipeline is a **multi-stage information retrieval funnel**, not a single `cosine_similarity` lookup. Dense bi-encoder embeddings (BGE-M3, `text-embedding-3-large`) capture synonyms (`memory leak` <-> `OOM killer`), while sparse lexical search (**BM25/SPLADE**) captures exact tokens (`ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_409`, `SKU-9040`).

**Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)**: $\text{score}(d) = \sum \frac{1}{k + \text{rank}_i(d)}$ ($k=60$) merges both rankings without score-normalization tuning, and a **cross-encoder reranker** narrows top-50 candidates down to the top-5 highest-precision chunks.

sectionDiagram.title: Pre-Filtered Hybrid Recall -> RRF Fusion -> Cross-Encoder Rerank
sectionDiagram.summary: Hybrid recall + RRF + cross-encoder reranking boosts NDCG@5 by 8–15% while shrinking prompt token costs.

learningJourney.title: Why Naive Vector Top-5 Fails (ACLs, Shredded Tables & Lost-in-the-Middle)
learningJourney.explanation: Naive "500-char fixed split + dense top-5" pipelines fail in three predictable ways: (1) **Post-retrieval ACL starvation**: filtering `tenant_id` *after* top-K search returns 0 results if another tenant's docs dominated top-K; (2) **Context shredding**: fixed character splits sever Markdown tables or `NOT recommended` caveats from their headers; (3) **Lost-in-the-middle**: stuffing 25 unranked chunks into the prompt degrades LLM attention.

learningJourney.title: Where Hybrid RAG shines (and where Prompt Caching or SQL win)
learningJourney.explanation: Use multi-stage RAG for large, mutable enterprise corpora; skip chunking when the entire corpus fits in prompt cache or requires SQL aggregation.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Multi-Tenant Docs, Runbooks & Support KBs
benefits: Handles millions of changing docs with strict index-level RBAC pre-filtering and exact error-code recall.
costs: Requires maintaining synchronized dense HNSW and inverted BM25 indices plus ~40–90 ms rerank latency.

benefits: Stuffing the full corpus into a provider prompt cache gives 100% recall with zero chunking loss.
costs: Unnecessary vector-DB infrastructure for tiny datasets.

benefits: Use Text-to-SQL or typed tool APIs instead of unstructured text chunks.
costs: Top-K chunk retrieval cannot compute exact sums across 10,000 rows.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How RRF Fusion & Offline Retrieval Evals are managed
learningJourney.explanation: Always decouple **retrieval evals** (`Recall@20`, `NDCG@5`, `MRR` on a 100–300 query golden set) from **generation evals**, enforce `tenant_id` / ACL filters inside the vector engine (`Qdrant`, `OpenSearch`, `pgvector`), and fuse dense + sparse lists via RRF (`k=60`).
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Dense-Only vs. Hybrid RRF vs. GraphRAG / Long Context
learningJourney.explanation: Balance recall quality, p99 latency, and ingestion complexity.

benefits: Best precision/recall balance across both semantic paraphrases and exact SKUs/codes.
costs: Adds ~40–90 ms reranker GPU latency and dual-index synchronization.
Misses exact identifiers, acronyms, and version numbers.

benefits: Zero chunk-boundary shredding on static handbooks or single codebases.
costs: Prohibitive token cost and TTFT latency on multi-million-document corpora.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production example: Multi-Tenant Hybrid Index with Parent Expansion
learningJourney.explanation: An enterprise support copilot indexes 256-token child chunks in Qdrant (HNSW + sparse BM25 vectors) with `tenant_id` and `acl_groups` payload indexes, fuses top-50 candidates with RRF, reranks to top-5 with `bge-reranker-v2-m3`, and fetches 1,024-token parent blocks from Redis/Postgres.

knowledgeCheck.question: In a multi-tenant RAG system, why must `tenant_id` and ACL filters be applied as *pre-filters* inside the vector/lexical index rather than *post-filtering* the top-K results in application code?

options.text: Post-filtering can return zero results if the global top-K vectors belong to other tenants, starving authorized users
options.feedback: Correct: pre-filtering inside Qdrant, OpenSearch, or pgvector guarantees all K candidates belong to the authorized tenant.

options.text: Because cosine similarity cannot be computed on strings
options.feedback: Metadata filtering restricts candidate IDs; the issue is top-K starvation.

options.text: Because RRF requires `k=60` documents per tenant
options.feedback: `k=60` is the RRF smoothing constant, unrelated to tenant count.
